links.reason: Both measure நட்பு against the world, but Kuruntokai 3's earth, sky and water are the whole cosmos, not features of the hill (குறிஞ்சி appears only in the slope image), so the claim that each takes its scale from the lover's land holds only for Ainkurunuru 184 (கடல்அணிந்தன்று அவர் ஊரே ... கடலினும் பெரிது). The pairing is real but the teaches overreaches.

வலனேர்பு (line 4) is the same verb and side as Kar Narpathu's ஏரும் வலம், where the friend calls it ஐயந்தீர் காட்சி. Mullaippattu line 91 (விசயம் வெல்கொடி யுயரி வலனேர்பு) does close with the army rising on the right, so the frame of sign and fulfilment is in the Tamil.
உயிர்நோய்செய்யாமை and உறுநோய் மறத்தல் answer the couplet's உயிர்க்குறுகண் செய்யாமை and உற்றநோய் நோன்றல; the verse adds three more and closes இழிவன்று இனிது தவம், a reply the couplet does not make.

Kural 1088 marks wonder at the mismatch (ஒண்ணுதற் கோஒ ... பீடு), while Kuruntokai 95 explains the defeat by kind: நீரோரன்ன சாயல் ... தீயோரன்ன என் உரன் அவித்தன்று. The pairing shows two different accounts of the same undoing.

The verbal overlap is exact (துறைவன் துறந்து, இறை, முன்கை, வளை), and the difference is real: Ainkurunuru doubles துறந்தென துறந்து so the bangles copy him, while the Kural's தூற்றா makes them publish it.

Both verses give the chaste wife a predicate (மருந்து in 1, சாவா உடம்பு for the man who gained her in 16), but this is one subject listed twice in a list-book; the teaches mostly restates the two predicates.

The formula line is shared (சிறுகண் பன்றிப் பெருஞ்சின ஒருத்தல், with துறுகல் in line 2 of each), but neither poem judges the boar: Natrinai 386 leaves it as scene and Ainkurunuru 267's sense (பண்பில சொல்லும் தேறுதல் செத்தே) is uncertain, so 'admired or suspected' is read into the image. QUALIFIES does not fit.
links.text_issue: ainkurunuru:267 line 1 reads பறிப் for பன்றிப்

links.reason: அழுப என்ப அவன் பெண்டிர் and கழறுப என்ப அவன் பெண்டிர் are the same formula. The wives are framed as தீயுறு மெழுகின் ஞெகிழ்வனர் in one and as a bard's பறையின் ஆனாது in the other, and the courtesan's reply grows from a count of days to கொண்டுகை வலித்தல் சூழ்ந்திசின்.

These are different situations, not incompatible claims: in 65 the rain is still being waited for, and in 338 the chariot has come. The note also misreads 65, where it is the rain (தான் வந்தன்றே தளிதரு தண்கார் ... இருந்திரோ எனவே) that seems to ask, not the stag that mocks. The tension is manufactured.

The rare simile is shared (சிரல்வாய்ச் செம்முகை / சிரல்வாய் வனப்பின) for the same தளவு bud. In 447 the bud's opening is the hoped-for hour (பிணிவீடு பெறுக மன்னவன் தொழிலே), and in Kar 36 it is seen on the way home, so it does mark the two ends of the wait.

The father's tall house and the danger are shared: தந்தை நெடுநகர் ஒருசிறை நின்றனென் in Akam 162 against துஞ்சுமனை நெடுநகர் வருதி ... தந்தைகை வேலே in Ainkurunuru 60. The man recalls the risk to his own heart, while the friend names it to him as a reason to stop.

Kural 750 concerns the defenders of a fort, and Patitruppattu 33's vehicle is a besieging army figured as a moving fort (வாள்மதில், வேல்மிளை, கால்வழங்கு ஆரெயில). That is a praise conceit, not an extension of the maxim, so 'takes that to its end' overstates a shared topic.

Akam 28 spells out the mechanism, அன்னை ... பிறர்த் தந்து நிறுக்குவள் ... உறற்கு அரிது ஆகும், which Ainkurunuru 260 compresses into பெறற்கரிது ... விளைந்தன தினையே. The pair shows what the four-line poem leaves implicit.

Akam 86 describes the rite with the same man (தருமணல் ஞெமிரி, தமர்தர), and nothing in it claims that a rite binds against a prior secret union. Kali 114's girl rejects a wedding (இரு மணம்) in a corrupt text. The verses treat different situations, so there is no incompatible claim, and the teaches builds a doctrine on a damaged poem.
links.text_issue: kalittokai:114 has lacunae at lines 2 and 18; lines 7-13 and 16-21 are absent from one source, and lines 1-2 do not fit

links.reason: The verbal mirror is real (என்னொடு புரையுநள் அல்லள் / தன்னொடு புரையுநர் against தன்னொடு நிகரா என்னொடு நிகரி), but the fragment is unframed and belongs to a puram book, so 'makes it likely the fragment is such a speech' is speculation built on the parallel.

The friend's பசலை மற்று என்னாங்கொல் ... ஈதோ நமர்வருவர் implies the news will banish the pallor. Kural 1265's காண்கமன் ... கண்டபின் நீங்கும் ... பசப்பு makes only sight the cure, which is a defensible conflict over the same pallor.

Both wives refuse the bard with irony: Naladiyar's கரும்பின் கடைக்கண் / இடைக்கண் and Thinaimozhi's எங்கையர். Naladiyar 390 sits in the chapter on chaste wives, so the didactic book does file the sharp tongue under karpu, which neither poem shows alone.

Ainkurunuru 433 only praises the road as having a forest that met கார்ப்பெயல். It neither reads a flowering as a sign nor argues about one, so 'what the waiting woman and her friend argued over' is constructed. The link is a shared season sign.

The name and epithet connection is real: நசைபிழைப்பு அறியாக் கழல்தொடி அதிகன் answers 101's பொய்யாகாதே. But a single use does not make a 'fixed epithet of the house', 'had become' asserts a chronology the poems do not give, and the note does not say what Paranar does with the name, which is to set the hard-to-win girl on the hill of the never-failing giver.

Puram 72 stakes இரப்போர்க்கு ஈயா இன்மை and புலவர் பாடாது வரைக with Maangudi Maruthan named as chief poet. Maduraikkanchi, by that poet about the same king, shows வரையா வாயில் and பாணர் வருக ... யாணர்ப் புலவரொடு, so the vow and its keeping are set side by side.

The girl herself cites the maxim as common speech (சான்றோர் கடன் நிலை குன்றலும் இலர் என்று ... உலகம் கூறுவது), which matches Kural 990's சான்றவர் சான்றாண்மை குன்றின். She stakes her life on it (சாதலும் இனிதே), which is what the teaches says the pair shows.

The structure of உதவி measured against earth and heaven is shared: Kural 101 has வையகமும் வானகமும், and Thinaimalai 62 has ஒரோஉதவி ... வேலாழி சூழுலகில் ... சுவர்கத்து உளராயின். The venba turns the measure of repayment into a measure of the helper.

The memory-versus-argument contrast is apt (வினை முடித்தன்ன இனியோள் against புணரின் புணராது பொருளே), but Natrinai 3's refusal and the heart urging the journey come from the colophon (பின்னும் பொருள் கடைக்கூட்டிய நெஞ்சிற்கு), not from the poem, which only asks உள்ளினென் அல்லெனோ.
This is the same neythal situation of refusing the bard. Natrinai 167's compliments are barbed (பயன் தெரி பனுவல் பை தீர் பாண), so 'courtesy' is generous; the range of tone is true but thin.

The verbal echo is clear (வேந்துவினை முடினே / வேந்தன் வினையு முடிந்தன), but the two moments of the king's work pending and done are the ordinary sequence of the pasarai situation; the teaches restates the narrative.

The refusal is the same (துன்னலம் ... பிறர்த் தோய்ந்த மார்பே / நண்ணேன் ... மார்பு), but the ground shifts from touch to கண்ணின் பொதுஉண்பர். The Kural does call him பரத்த, yet its stated reason is the glances, so the sharpening is real.

The formula is shared (வாரார் ஆயினோ நன்று), but the contrast is false: Natrinai 255 also has the sleepless watchers (கானவர் துஞ்சார், line 3), and Kuruntokai 375's drum sounds when the tiger (இரவரி) comes. Both poems carry both reasons.
பழிநமக் கெழுக என்னாய் with Vanan's விழுநிதி is the Kural's பழிமலைந்து எய்திய ஆக்கம் refused, and ஈதல் உள்ளமொடு இசைவேட்குவை adds the giving the couplet omits.

The stag is described in near-identical words (திரிமருப் பிரலை அண்ணல் / இருதிரி மருப்பின் அண்ணல் இரலை), with its doe in both. In Akam 34 the stag's care moves the man to hurry (பெருந்தகைக்கு உடைந்த நெஞ்சம்), and in Kuruntokai 338 it stands beside வந்தன்று பெருவிறல் தேரே.

The same line, செய்வினை முடித்த செம்மல் உள்ளம், appears in both: in 270 it is the man's own state as he lies on her hair, and in 275 it is the friend's guess as she listens for the bell (தேர்மணி கொல்).

Paripadal 1.73 already has the discus-bearer pulling (ஆழியான் வாங்க), and the fragment is a hymn to the serpent, which credits him by design (தாம் ... தாம்). Thiruppugazh 11 is a Murugan song naming his uncle by stock epithets, so no shift in the myth over time can be read from the pair.
These are refrain variants within one decade (நாணிலை மன்ற பாண / பண்பிலை மன்ற பாண). The reading that he brings words where the man is wanted (சொல்உகுப்போய், கொண்கனைத் தாரா தோயே) is true but thin.

Thirumurugatruppadai's list already includes town festivals, crossroads and common grounds (ஊரூர் கொண்ட விழவு, சதுக்கமும் சந்தியும், மன்றமும்), not only the hills, and nothing dates one idyll before the other. The claimed movement of the rite from hills to city is unsupported.

The shared frame is real (குன்றுதல் உண்டோ மதுரை ... குன்றம் / கோத்தை உண்டாமோ ... வார்த்தை உண்டாகும் அளவு). But a 'move' ending in a 'last stanza' depends on the editorial order of collected fragments, and 'the poet's own stock' is an addition.

விருந்து அயர் விருப்பினள் ... திருந்திழை closes both poems: in 361 it follows அரும் படர் அகல நீக்கி, and in 374 it is joined to வருந்தும். The same formula carries joy or grief depending on the return.

Kural 661 names no assets. The note rests on what a commentator takes மற்றைய to mean, and the teaches, that the six assets are empty without the mind, is not what either couplet says; 661 says only that firmness in action is firmness of mind.

The astral image is shared (செல்வனொடு நிலைஇய உரோகிணி / திங்கட் சகடம் மண்டிய துகள்தீர் கூட்டத்து). But the queen's own wedding is nowhere in Nedunalvadai, so reading her sigh as a wedding memory needs a generous inference from one other poem.

கண்ணோட்டம் is shared, but lines 1-2 of the venba are uncertain: தீர்க்குதும் is first person plural, so the reading that the husband withholds the regard is not fixed by the Tamil. 'Already at work' rests on that construal.

Kainnilai 42's taunt (கூத்தனாக் கொண்டு ... ஆட்டுவித்து உண்ணினும் உண்) is about the bard profiting from the man, not about contrition. Joining it to 46's நாணினன் போன்றான் as 'performance from both sides' stretches the dancer word.

The protest is the same (அறியா வேலன் / தோற்றமல்லது நோய்க்கு மருந்தாகா), but the addressee differs: Ainkurunuru 243 speaks to the mother (மனம் கொள்குவை அனை), Kuruntokai 263 to the girl. The pair shows the objection turned toward the household.

The refrain இனிது மன்றஅவர் கிடக்கை takes two prices (ஈனும் உம்பரும் பெறலரும் / இவ்வுலகு உடன் உறுமே). The point that the hyperbole varies within the decade is true but slight, and QUALIFIES is a loose fit.

The image is shared closely, down to the words: a bear seeking prey (இரை தேர்) digs into the snake's mound (அரவின் ... புற்றம் / அர வாழ் புற்றம்), on the path to the meeting in 336 and the road away for wealth in 325. This gives the teaches' point that the danger lies on the road either way.
Both men give up the journey, but this is the shared situation. The claim about form (பணைத்தோள் விலங்கின செலவே against Akam 5's full scene) is true but generic.

poems.note: The tiger killing an elephant for its starving mate is an act, but what it implies for the lovers cannot be put in one sentence apart from the path's danger.

iraicchi.act: coos close by as if rebuking those who leave and saying not to go
iraicchi.sense: the birds voice the plea the heroine would make to the man not to leave her for wealth

poems.note: The poem states the sense with கழறுவ போல, so it barely rises from the carrier.
The heifer is an open simile (போல்).
The wind strewing ஞாழல் on neythal maps to no second part of the situation; the infant is an open simile.
The poem states the moral itself (மலை வாழ்நர் அல்ல புரிந்து ஒழுகலான்).

iraicchi.act: calls ceaselessly as if telling lovers who have united not to part and those who have parted to unite
iraicchi.sense: the season itself urges the sulking wife and straying husband to reunite

poems.note: Stated openly with என்பன போல, as in Natrinai 243.
The anril pair's cry is sound carrying mood; the shark breaking nets yields no second correspondence.

iraicchi.act: mistakes a stray rain for the rainy season and blooms
iraicchi.sense: the heroine weeping now mistakes the season too, and the man has not yet broken his promise

iraicchi.act: having lost its mate to a tiger, holds its calf and suffers like one with a deep wound
iraicchi.sense: the girl will suffer so if the man fails her, and the friend means him to hear it

poems.note: The wet cock is a look of the season, not an act.

iraicchi.act: having fed on the forked varagu ears, rests with its stag
iraicchi.sense: the man too will soon lie at rest beside his wife

poems.note: The elephant frightened by the arrow marks the danger of the path; no single implication for the lovers follows.

iraicchi.act: unable to bear its weary mate's distress, gores the yaa tree and gives her its moist fibre
iraicchi.sense: even beasts on the road he took care for their mates, yet he has forgotten her

iraicchi.act: guards the she-elephant that has just calved, with her calf
iraicchi.sense: the hill man will likewise come to wed and protect her

poems.note: Two pairs: the tusker that killed the tiger matches the man who won her, and its sleep after feeding, deaf to the falls, matches his forgetting.

ullurai.anchor: நல்கிய நாள்தவச் சிலவே அலரே ... ஆர்ப்பினும் பெரிதே

poems.note: The surf wrecking the crab's small house matches the gossip ruining the girl, and its drum-like roar matches the uproar of the talk.
The guarding elephant marks the path's danger; its implication for the lovers is unclear.

iraicchi.act: is cherished and attended by its mate as it comes
iraicchi.sense: the hill man does not cherish her as the tusker does his mate, so her shoulders lie as in hell

poems.note: Lines 1-2 are obscure and the agent of பேணி is unstated.

The crab leaving its mate matches the husband leaving the wife, and its cutting the tender vallai stems matches his harm to the women; the single creature carries a mapped scene, so this is ullurai, not iraicchi.
The heron crushing the அடும்பு flowers to eat fish matches the man who spoiled her beauty for his pleasure; the second pair is thin.
